# lumos_integration_connection_schema (Data Source)

IntegrationConnectionSchema DataSource

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "lumos_integration_connection_schema" "my_integrationconnectionschema" {
  app_class_id = "...my_app_class_id..."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_class_id` (String) Canonical identifier of the integration the schema is for (echoes the request).

### Read-Only

- `auth_schema` (Attributes) JSON Schema (draft-07 style) describing the `auth` object to pass to `POST /apps`. Properties are the credential keys the integration accepts; secret fields are marked `writeOnly`, and fixed-choice fields carry an `enum`. Most integrations use a flat object with credential keys at the top level; some nest credentials under named groups when the integration supports multiple authentication methods — mirror that nesting in the connect request. An empty object (`{"type":"object","properties":{} }`) means no credentials are supplied up front (the connection is completed via browser consent in the Lumos UI). A manually-set instance id belongs in `settings_schema`, not `auth`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth_schema))
- `settings_schema` (Attributes) JSON Schema of the non-secret `settings` object for `POST /apps`. Carries tenant URLs, routing configuration, and other non-secret values the integration needs beyond credentials. Some integrations require a manually-set instance id as `app_instance_identifier` (e.g. an Okta domain); others derive it from the credentials during connect. Integrations that run through an on-prem agent take `on_prem_agent_cluster_id` here. Integrations that need no non-secret configuration return an empty object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings_schema))
